_meta: A sequence of agent turns, each with a tool call, the observation the MODEL wrote for itself in its output, and the REAL result the tool returns when actually executed, used to show why the harness must execute the tool call and supply the real observation rather than trusting the observation the model narrated -- because a model will sometimes write out a plausible result instead of (or alongside) calling the tool, and if the harness feeds that self-written result back as if it were real, the model is reasoning over data it invented. In a tool-using loop the model emits an action (a tool call) and the harness is supposed to run it and return what the tool actually produced. But models, trained on text that shows tool calls followed by their outputs, will happily continue the pattern by writing the output too -- an 'Observation: ...' line the model made up. That narrated observation is just generated text; it is not grounded in any real execution, so it can be confidently wrong. The harness's job is to treat the model's output as a request to act, extract only the action, run the tool itself, and inject the tool's genuine result as the observation, discarding whatever the model claimed the result was. Trust the model's version and it grades its own homework: it fabricates a result, reads its own fabrication back, and builds the rest of the run on fiction, with no error anywhere. turns lists each turn with the tool call, the model's claimed observation, and the tool's real output. These are the fixture; under a harness that trusts the model's claim vs one that executes and uses the real output, the observations used and the fabrications are computed.
